case_study_insert.main_stem: Rothermere Marine Instruments (RMI) is a partnership in the marine electronics sector, employing a workforce of 50. Founded in 2008 by senior partner Innes Rothermere, the firm produces navigation displays and depth gauges for commercial fishing and leisure boats, and operates a hierarchical structure with autocratic leadership. RMI plans to invest $760,000 in a new display-assembly line, financed by $360,000 retained profit and $400,000 through hire purchase. It has fixed costs of $245,000 a year, a variable cost of $8.00 a unit and a selling price of $15.00, and currently produces 70,000 units a year. RMI faces two operational problems: a defect rate of 3.4% on assembled displays and longer delivery times, with labour turnover rising among test technicians.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations Log — Q3 2025: The assembly line built 16,800 marine displays last quarter at a defect rate of 3.4%, up from 2.1% a year earlier. Customer complaints rose from 22 to 39 a month and average delivery time stretched from 3.0 to 5.6 days. A survey of 520 boat owners found 61% would pay up to $0.60 more for a waterproof display and 44% check warranty terms before buying. Records show 12 of 50 technicians have not completed on-the-job training on the new test rigs; external certification courses cost $640 per employee.
case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 4.0% to 4.75%, raising the cost of variable-rate borrowing. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 4.8% from $13.00 to $13.62 an hour from April 2026. (3) Imported electronic display components have risen 11.3% in cost year-on-year, shipping freight inflation is 6.4%, and recreational boat registrations grew 3.1% over the same period.

questions.question_text: RMI plans to finance $400,000 of its $760,000 display-assembly line through hire purchase rather than retained profit. Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for RMI of using hire purchase.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Hire purchase spreads the $400,000 cost of the new display-assembly line into manageable instalments, so RMI can install the equipment now and begin producing displays rather than waiting to build up cash. This preserves the $360,000 retained profit for working capital and helps a 50-person partnership protect its $15.00 selling price and the $7.00 contribution on each of 70,000 units while it tackles the 3.4% defect rate.

Disadvantage: Hire purchase is more expensive overall than paying cash because interest is built into the instalments, raising the true cost of the $760,000 investment and adding a fixed commitment alongside $245,000 a year of fixed costs. If delivery times lengthen and cash is tied up in the 16,800 displays built last quarter, missed instalments could put the equipment at risk, reducing Innes Rothermere's control over the new line.

The partnership can therefore keep the $7.00 contribution on 70,000 displays intact while it fixes the 3.4% defect rate, rather than spending part of each sale on hire-purchase interest.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage of hire purchase.
1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage of hire purchase.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to RMI's expansion, cash flow, contribution and defect rate.
Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to RMI's instalments, retained profit and control.

questions.question_text: RMI is launching its new waterproof navigation displays. Consider advertising in boating magazines, sponsoring a national boat show, or e-commerce through a new website. Which should RMI choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Boating magazine advertising: Print adverts in fishing and leisure boating titles reach exactly the owners RMI supplies and can show the $0.60 premium accepted by 61% of the 520 surveyed boat owners. However, readership is seasonal and narrow, adverts are costly to place repeatedly, and a static page cannot answer the 44% who check warranty terms before buying, so response is hard to measure for a 50-employee partnership.

National boat show sponsorship: A stand lets buyers see the waterproof display and ask Innes Rothermere's team about warranty, which directly addresses the 44% who check terms and helps overcome concern over a 3.4% defect rate. Yet stand and travel costs are high beside a $760,000 assembly-line investment, the event lasts only a few days, and it draws leisure owners rather than the commercial fishing buyers who sustain 70,000 units a year.

E-commerce through a new website: A website can display warranty details and specifications to the 44% who check them, take orders nationally and track enquiries, while the 61% willing to pay $0.60 more can be offered the waterproof upgrade at checkout. It avoids print and exhibition costs and supports the launch after the 5.6-day delivery problem is fixed, though it needs digital skills and steady web traffic to deliver sales.

Recommendation: RMI should choose e-commerce through a new website. It reaches buyers cost-effectively, answers warranty questions and can be measured against the 70,000-unit target. Magazines are rejected as narrow and unmeasurable; the boat show is rejected as short-lived and expensive. RMI can add a small show presence once online demand is proven.

questions.question_text: RMI's defect rate has risen to 3.4% and delivery times have stretched to 5.6 days. Explain two benefits for RMI of its hierarchical structure with autocratic leadership in addressing these problems.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: A hierarchical structure gives RMI a clear chain of command, so Innes Rothermere can issue one consistent instruction to test technicians when the defect rate reaches 3.4%, tightening inspection routines across the 16,800 displays built last quarter without conflicting messages. This top-down control suits a partnership whose senior partner must coordinate commercial and leisure customers quickly.

Point 2: Autocratic leadership enables fast decisions to clear the 5.6-day delivery backlog, for example by reallocating the 12 of 50 technicians still awaiting on-the-job training to the test rigs or authorising overtime, without lengthy consultation. Under Taylor's ideas of clear method and supervision, quicker decisions protect the $7.00 contribution on 70,000 units, though RMI should watch that rising labour turnover among technicians is not made worse by a directive style.

In a partnership the senior partner remains accountable to the other owners, so a clear chain of command also makes it easier to explain to clients why delivery times have stretched to 5.6 days and what is being done about it, supporting the 61% of surveyed owners who would pay $0.60 more for a waterproof display.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit of hierarchy/autocratic leadership (max 2).
1 mark for each valid benefit of hierarchy/autocratic leadership (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation linked to RMI's defect rate, delivery time and output.
Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation linked to RMI's decisions, technicians and contribution.

questions.question_text: RMI must strengthen its testing team to cut the 3.4% defect rate. Consider internal recruitment or external recruitment. Which should RMI choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
Internal recruitment: Promoting an existing assembly worker into testing is cheap, quick and low-risk because RMI already knows the person's reliability and they understand the 16,800 displays built each quarter. It can also motivate the 50-strong workforce by showing a promotion route. However, internal candidates may lack the technical knowledge for the new test rigs, and the 12 of 50 technicians still needing on-the-job training show the current skill base is thin; promoting without proper certification courses at $640 each could leave the 3.4% defect rate unchanged.

External recruitment: Hiring experienced test technicians brings proven diagnostic skills and fresh methods, which can attack the rise from 2.1% to 3.4% defects and help shorten the 5.6-day delivery time. The costs are higher — advertising, interviewing and a longer settling-in period — and an outsider may take time to learn RMI's autocratic routines, so the benefit is not immediate.

Decision: RMI should choose external recruitment for the specialist testing roles. The technical skill gap is the direct cause of the defect problem, and internal promotion alone cannot close it; internal recruitment is rejected as too limited in skill, while short external courses at $640 can then update the whole team. RMI should still use internal promotion for supervisory positions to keep morale high.

RMI should also set a probation period with a practical test on the new rigs so the 3.4% defect rate is actually reduced, and combine it with the $640 certification courses for existing staff. Without such checks, hiring an outsider would raise costs without fixing the 5.6-day delivery problem, and the partnership would gain little from the decision.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how RMI's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $245,000 ÷ ($15.00 − $8.00) = $245,000 ÷ $7.00 = 35,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 35,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $15.00 − $8.00 = $7.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $7.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways RMI's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare break-even of 35,000 units with output of 70,000 units: the margin of safety is 35,000 units, showing how far sales can fall before the display line loses money.
2. Use the $7.00 contribution to test a $0.60 waterproof upgrade; managers can judge whether extra units offset the cost of reworking displays at a 3.4% defect rate.
3. Check that $7.00 contribution on 70,000 units can cover the $400,000 hire-purchase commitment and the $245,000 fixed costs before RMI expands further.
4. Monitor unit cost of $245,000 ÷ 70,000 + $8.00 = $11.50 each quarter to spot waste from defects and rising imported component prices.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 35,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $7.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses: margin of safety 35,000 units; waterproof-upgrade pricing; hire-purchase affordability; and unit-cost benchmarking at $11.50.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark for each valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate RMI's financial position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has RMI's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.60 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.54 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 1.10 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 0.92 : 1

Detailed workings: In 2024 current assets were $100,000 inventories + $160,000 trade receivables + $60,000 cash = $320,000, and $320,000 ÷ $200,000 current liabilities gives the 2024 measure. In 2025 the corresponding assets were $150,000 + $180,000 + $40,000 = $370,000, and $370,000 ÷ $240,000 gives the 2025 measure. For the stock-excluding measure the 2024 numerator is $320,000 − $100,000 = $220,000, and $220,000 ÷ $200,000 = 1.10; in 2025 $370,000 − $150,000 = $220,000 and $220,000 ÷ $240,000 = 0.92.

Evaluation: Liquidity has deteriorated on both measures. The broad coverage measure slipped from 1.60 to 1.54 as current liabilities rose from $200,000 to $240,000 faster than assets, while cash fell from $60,000 to $40,000. The stock-excluding measure fell further, from 1.10 to 0.92, because inventories built up from $100,000 to $150,000; RMI is increasingly relying on selling stock to meet short-term debts at the very time it is funding a $760,000 display line with hire purchase. Rising receivables of $180,000 add to the cash strain if leisure boat owners pay late.

Conclusion: RMI's financial position has not improved; it has weakened. Both the 2024–2025 measures (1.60 to 1.54 and 1.10 to 0.92) fell, and the decline is concentrated in cash and inventory rather than a one-off. RMI should reduce stock and tighten credit control before adding further hire-purchase commitments.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for RMI of launching a new e-commerce website for direct sales.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: A website lets RMI show warranty details and specifications to the 44% of 520 surveyed boat owners who check terms before buying, and offer the $0.60 waterproof upgrade to the 61% who value it. Direct online orders can lift sales beyond the current 70,000 units without the cost of a boat-show stand, protecting the $7.00 contribution per display while the $760,000 assembly line beds in.

Disadvantage: Building and promoting a website adds cost and needs digital skills that a 50-person partnership may have to buy in, while the current 5.6-day delivery time and 3.4% defect rate could turn online buyers into complainants — complaints have already risen from 22 to 39 a month. If orders grow faster than the test rigs can clear them, RMI's reputation for reliable navigation displays suffers just as it invests $760,000 in new capacity.

With a 50-person workforce, the website should be promoted through boating forums so it reaches the 520 surveyed owners efficiently; otherwise the $0.60 premium message may not be seen.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage of e-commerce.
1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage of e-commerce.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to RMI's survey, defects, complaints and investment.
Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to RMI's delivery time and skills.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the rise in the base interest rate to 4.75%, the 4.8% minimum wage increase and the 11.3% rise in imported display component costs will affect RMI. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.0% to 4.75%): RMI's $400,000 of hire purchase may carry costs linked to interest rates, but the insert does not state the agreement's terms, so any figure is only an illustrative bound: a full 0.75 percentage-point rise on $400,000 is 0.0075 × $400,000 = $3,000 a year. That is modest beside $245,000 fixed costs, although dearer credit could slow boat buyers and future expansion.

Minimum wage increase (4.8%, to $13.62 an hour): RMI employs 50 people and the rise feeds into wage costs, but the insert gives no hours worked or pay rates, so an annual total cannot be invented. The honest test is productivity: 70,000 units ÷ 50 staff = 1,400 units per worker. A higher wage is affordable only if that productivity holds or output rises; otherwise unit labour costs eat into the $7.00 contribution.

Component cost inflation (11.3%): The $8.00 variable cost is not broken down in the insert, so only a bound is possible — if the whole variable cost rose 11.3% it would add 0.113 × $8.00 = $0.904 a unit, about 70,000 × $0.904 = $63,280 a year. Even a partial rise reduces contribution and raises the 35,000-unit break-even, though the $0.60 premium wanted by 61% of buyers offers some recovery.

Conclusion: The 11.3% rise in imported components will have the greatest impact. It applies to every one of the 70,000 displays and directly erodes the $7.00 contribution needed to fund the $760,000 line. The interest effect is at most a bounded $3,000, and the wage effect depends on productivity, so neither matches pervasive component inflation.
